info.name: Applicant and Credential Services
info.description:
Run in order against the team stack (docker compose up). The setup folder opens a real session through Player and Session, so the session tokens are the real ones.

Everything goes through the Gateway. A client sends Authorization: Bearer <token>; the Gateway validates it, drops the header and tells the service who is calling through X-Player-Id, X-Session-Id and X-Session-Role. Only the last folder sets those headers itself, to check that the Gateway does not believe them.

The endpoints the contract marks internal, here opening a session, creating an applicant, which Applicant does by saga, reading the full applicant with the impostor flag, and validating documents, are refused by the Gateway, which has no internal port any more: services call each other through the Message Broker. Their requests here go to the services themselves on the Docker backend network, at sessionServiceBaseUrl, applicantServiceBaseUrl and credentialServiceBaseUrl, which nothing publishes. Reaching them means running inside the Docker network:

    docker run --rm --network pad-team-20_backend -v "$PWD/postman:/etc/newman" \
      postman/newman run applicant-and-credential.postman_collection.json \
      --env-var gatewayBaseUrl=http://gateway:8000

Run it from your machine instead and the internal requests cannot reach the services: they fail, and so does every request that needs the session or the applicants they create.

Folders 4 and 5 talk to the Message Broker, also from inside the network: Session's `CreateApplicant` as an envelope, and the saga coordinator's `POST /sagas` and `GET /sagas/{id}`.

item.name: 4. Through the broker
item.description:
Session does not call `POST /applicants` through the Gateway any more. It names the operation `CreateApplicant` and the Message Broker picks an instance of `applicant` from the registry, so the caller never holds an address and carries no circuit breaker of its own.

The broker publishes no port, so these run from inside the Docker network, like the internal requests above.

item.name: 5. The saga coordinator
item.description:
Lab 5: the broker coordinates the saga that creates an applicant in Credential, University Record and Applicant. These requests drive the coordinator directly, on `POST /sagas` and `GET /sagas/{id}`, with Credential as the only participant, so they leave nothing behind.

The first saga keeps a real slice in Credential, an applicant with no documents, and its second step sends Credential a body without the story, which Credential refuses with `422`. A refusal is final, so the coordinator undoes the steps already done, newest first: `DeleteApplicant` removes the slice, and the saga ends `compensated`.

Like folder 4, these run from inside the Docker network: the broker publishes no port.

request.description: The coordinator runs the steps in order. Step 2 is refused, so it runs the compensation of step 1. `waitSeconds` lets the POST wait for the end: `201` once the saga has finished, `202` if not yet.
